sentences.text:
[1] The present successive bail application is filed by the applicant - accused under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with FIR being C.R.
No.11216007210243 of 2021 registered with Sector 21 Police Station, Gandhinagar for offence under Sections 406, 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.
[2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Yash Patel for the applicant and learned A.P.P. Mr. Bhargav Pandya for the respondent - State of Gujarat.

[3] At the out, it is to be noted that the present one is a serious scam wherein the applicant - accused, by forging and fabricating letter heads NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/8479/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined and seals of high officials of the police department, collected money from the students.

Be that as it may, the present application is a successive bail application thereby when a pertinent question was asked to the learned advocate for the applicant that what is the change in circumstances after rejection of the earlier bail vide order dated 12 th May 2022 on merits and with reasoned order, to which learned advocate for the Siddharthbhai Hiteshbhai Pathak vs State Of Gujarat on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147365684/
1 applicant has fairly admitted that as such there is no change in circumstances, however, made an attempt to persuade this Court by referring some evidences recorded before the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [4] In view of the aforesaid, it is a settled principle of law that the successive bail applications are not to be entertained casually, but the only in the circumstances when there is a material change in the circumstances.
In the present case, learned advocate for the applicant was unable to show any material change or rather admitted that there is no change in the circumstances.

So far as the evidences recorded by the Trial Court is concerned, in my considered opinion, while exercising power under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C., more particularly, when the Trial Court is fully seized of the matter, it would not be in the fitness of thing to evaluate the evidence which otherwise yet to be evaluated by the Trial Court.

At this stage, it would be apt to refer to and rely upon NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/8479/2024 ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 undefined the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kalyan Chandra Sarkar vs. Rajesh Ranjan reported in (2005)
2 SCC 42.
